title: E3SM User Guide: Overview
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: The E3SM User Guide introduces the Energy Exascale Earth System Model and collects practical documentation for configuring cases, components, input data, builds, runs, output, and analysis. It is the preferred starting point for users who need authoritative model workflow guidance.

title: E3SM User Guide: Cases
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: An E3SM case is a configured model experiment created from a compset, grid, machine, compiler, and project options. Case directories contain XML settings, namelists, build scripts, run scripts, and provenance needed to reproduce the configuration.

title: E3SM User Guide: Compsets
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: Compsets define the science component set and forcing choices for an E3SM case. They select active, data, stub, or prescribed components for atmosphere, land, ocean, sea ice, river, and other model systems.

title: E3SM User Guide: Grids
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: Grid aliases specify horizontal and sometimes vertical discretizations used by E3SM components. A case grid must be compatible with the selected compset and available mapping files and input data.

title: Running E3SM: create_newcase
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: The create_newcase command creates a case using required selections such as case name, compset, resolution, machine, and project account. After creation, users normally run case.setup before building and submitting the case.

title: Running E3SM: case.setup
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: case.setup generates case infrastructure including build and run scripts, user namelist files, and component configuration files. It should be rerun when relevant XML settings change before the model is built.

title: Running E3SM: case.build
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: case.build compiles the E3SM executable for the selected machine, compiler, compset, and grid. Build failures are commonly investigated by checking environment modules, Macros, compiler output, and component build logs.

title: Running E3SM: case.submit
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: case.submit submits the model run through the machine batch system after setup and build are complete. The command writes run logs and manages continuation according to case XML settings such as STOP_OPTION, STOP_N, and REST_OPTION.

title: Running E3SM: XML Changes
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: xmlchange updates case XML variables such as run length, wallclock time, project, queue, tasks, threads, and component layout. Many XML changes require rerunning case.setup so generated scripts match the new configuration.

title: Running E3SM: Namelists
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: User namelist files in a case directory customize component runtime options. The preview_namelists workflow lets users inspect generated namelists before submitting a run. Namelist changes should be documented with the case for provenance.

title: Running E3SM: Restarts
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: Restart files allow an E3SM simulation to continue from a saved model state. REST_OPTION and REST_N control restart frequency, while CONTINUE_RUN and RUN_REFCASE related settings are used for continuing or branching cases.

title: Running E3SM: Output and Archives
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: E3SM writes history, restart, log, and timing output under run and archive directories configured by the case. Short-term archiving moves completed output from the run directory to structured component archive locations.

title: EAM Documentation: Overview
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: The E3SM Atmosphere Model, EAM, represents atmospheric dynamics, physics parameterizations, aerosols, clouds, radiation, and coupling to other Earth system components. EAM configuration is controlled by compsets, grids, namelists, and build options.

title: EAM Documentation: Physics
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: EAM configuration documentation describes atmosphere model settings controlled by compsets, grids, namelists, build options, and physics parameterizations. EAM physics covers cloud macrophysics, microphysics, convection, turbulence, aerosols, radiation, and surface exchange. Scientific changes to physics settings should be paired with diagnostics and reproducible case metadata.

title: EAM Documentation: History Output
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: Atmosphere history output controls which EAM variables are written and at what frequency. Users commonly adjust fincl, fexcl, nhtfrq, and mfilt style namelist controls to add variables or change output cadence.

title: EAMxx Documentation: Overview
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: EAMxx is the performance-portable atmosphere model infrastructure for E3SM using C++ and Kokkos-based approaches. It supports atmosphere processes, grids, fields, diagnostics, and coupling patterns designed for modern accelerated architectures.

title: EAMxx Documentation: Input YAML
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: EAMxx runtime configuration commonly uses YAML input files to define atmosphere process settings, output streams, diagnostics, and field requests. YAML changes should remain consistent with the selected compset and build configuration.

title: EAMxx Documentation: Diagnostics
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: EAMxx diagnostics derive additional atmosphere fields from model state and process outputs. Diagnostics can be requested in output configuration so users can analyze quantities that are not directly prognostic variables.

title: ELM Documentation: Overview
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: The E3SM Land Model, ELM, simulates terrestrial water, energy, carbon, vegetation, soil, and biogeochemical processes. ELM is configured through compsets, land surface data, namelists, and coupling to atmosphere and river components.

title: ELM Documentation: Surface Data
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: ELM surface datasets describe land units, soil properties, vegetation, topography, and other spatial inputs required by land simulations. Surface data must match the land grid and experiment assumptions used by the case.

title: ELM Documentation: Parameters
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: ELM parameter files provide values for land model process representations. Changing parameter files can alter hydrology, vegetation, carbon, and energy behavior, so experiments should preserve parameter provenance and use diagnostics to evaluate impacts.

title: ELM Documentation: History Output
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: ELM history output records land variables for analysis, including hydrology, carbon, energy, vegetation, and soil fields. Users select output variables and frequencies through land model namelist and history controls.

title: E3SM Diagnostics: Overview
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM diagnostics documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: E3SM Diagnostics, often run with e3sm_diags, provides standardized analysis and plotting for model output against observations or reference simulations. Atmosphere diagnostics document diagnostic plots, variables, seasons, regions, and metrics for evaluating atmosphere model behavior. It also supports ocean, sea ice, land, and other diagnostic sets depending on available data.

title: E3SM Diagnostics: Parameters
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM diagnostics documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: e3sm_diags uses parameter files to specify test data paths, reference data paths, output locations, seasons, regions, variables, and diagnostic sets. Parameter files make diagnostic runs repeatable and easier to share.

title: E3SM Diagnostics: Running Diagnostics
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM diagnostics documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: Diagnostics are run after model output is available and typically require paths to climatology or time-series files. Generated output includes plots, metrics, and web-viewable pages that summarize model behavior against references.

title: E3SM Diagnostics: Viewer
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM diagnostics documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: The diagnostics viewer organizes plots and tables so users can inspect generated results by set, variable, season, and region. Viewer output should be archived with simulation metadata when supporting scientific conclusions.

title: E3SM-Unified: Overview
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM-Unified documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: E3SM-Unified is a conda-based environment maintained for E3SM workflows and for building a consistent E3SM software stack for analysis. It bundles common Python packages and E3SM analysis tools so users can run diagnostics and post-processing with a consistent software stack.

title: E3SM-Unified: Activation
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM-Unified documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: Users activate an E3SM-Unified environment before running bundled analysis tools. On supported machines, module or activation instructions identify the available environment version and prepare PATH and Python dependencies.

title: E3SM-Unified: Included Tools
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM-Unified documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: E3SM-Unified includes analysis and workflow packages used by the project, such as diagnostics, post-processing, xarray-based tools, plotting libraries, and scientific Python dependencies. Exact packages vary by environment release.

title: E3SM-Unified: Troubleshooting
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM-Unified documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: When an E3SM-Unified command fails, users should confirm the intended environment is active, check module conflicts, verify input paths, and compare the tool version with the environment release documented for the machine.

title: E3SM User Guide: Provenance and Reproducibility
provenance: Curated static excerpt from official E3SM documentation for phase 1 tests.
text: Reproducible E3SM experiments preserve case XML settings, user namelists, source code revision, machine and compiler choices, input data versions, run scripts, logs, restart files, diagnostics, and notes about intentional changes.
